title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continuing from p.527). Grothendieck studies a homomorphism Psi from Ñ_{1,1} (a profinite 'Teichmüller-type' group in genus 1 with one marked point, of GT/Galois type) to a profinite group G. Its image contains a quotient 𝔊 of SL(2,Z)^ (profinite completion), generated by the images ρ, σ of the standard elliptic generators. These satisfy ρ^6 = σ^4 = 1 and ρ^3 = σ^2 = '-1', which is central and involutive. For u in Ñ_{1,1}(ω), one gets lifts α̃, β̃ (determined up to sign) and elements ξ, η with u(ρ) = ξρ and u(σ) = ησ.

This page fixes a difficulty. In general α̃ is only known to lie in GL(2,Z)^, not in SL(2,Z)^. One must therefore bring in an element τ of GL(2,Z)^ of determinant -1 and its action on 𝔊.

He sets ε0 = σρ and ε1 = ρσ, the two standard parabolic ('cusp') generators. Writing x(y) for conjugation x y x^{-1}, one has ε1 = σ(ε0) = ρ(ε0). Using σ^{-1} = -σ, also ε0 = -σ^{-1}ρ and ε1 = -ρσ^{-1}.

The outer involution τ is defined by (25): τ(σ) = σ^{-1} and τ(ρ) = σρ^{-1}σ^{-1}. Concretely this is conjugation by a determinant -1 matrix in GL2, the 'complex conjugation' / real structure on the modular curve, which inverts parabolics.

From (24) and (22) one deduces (26): τ(ε0) = ε0^{-1} and τ(ε1) = ε1^{-1}.

He then forms the semidirect product ('½ direct') 𝔊' := {1,τ}⋉𝔊, the analogue of GL(2,Z)^ ⊃ SL(2,Z)^. He announces that he will paraphrase constructions already made elsewhere.

The next page (section IV) restarts axiomatically. It takes a profinite 𝔊 with generators ρ, σ satisfying these relations and τ an automorphism as in (25). It then defines B_{ρ,σ} ⊂ Aut(𝔊)×Ẑ* by conditions of the shape u(ε0) = ε0^μ, with u(σ) and u(ρ) conjugate to σ^μ and ρ^μ. This is a GT-like group attached to an arbitrary finite or profinite quotient of SL2(Z)^, i.e. a 'variation on the loop equation' in genus 1.
errors: No errors in the computations. Checks: τ^2 = id. τ preserves ρ^6 = σ^4 = 1 and ρ^3 = σ^2. τ(ε0) = σ^{-1}·σρ^{-1}σ^{-1} = ρ^{-1}σ^{-1} = ε0^{-1}. τ(ε1) = σρ^{-1}σ^{-2} = -σρ^{-1} = σ^{-1}ρ^{-1} = ε1^{-1}.

Gap: for an arbitrary quotient 𝔊 of SL(2,Z)^, τ descends to 𝔊 only if the kernel is τ-stable. The page tacitly assumes this ('l'action de τ dans 𝔊 sur 𝔊'). The next page makes it explicit ('passe au quotient').

ideas.what: Use the outer involution τ (det -1 element of GL2(Z)^) acting on SL2(Z)^-quotients by σ↦σ^{-1}, ρ↦σρ^{-1}σ^{-1}, inverting both cusp generators ε0 = σρ and ε1 = ρσ
ideas.modern_name: action of GL2(Z) ⊃ SL2(Z) by an orientation-reversing involution; complex conjugation on the moduli of elliptic curves / Γ_{1,1}

ideas.what: Semidirect product 𝔊' = {1,τ}⋉𝔊, the analogue of GL2(Z)^ for quotients of SL2(Z)^, used to handle lifts that lie only in GL2(Z)^ when defining a genus-1 GT-type action
ideas.modern_name: extended (orientation-reversing) mapping class group in genus 1; GT action on Γ_{1,1}^ with λ ∈ Ẑ*
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nakamura; Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps; Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps (genus-1 relations for GT)

missed.claim: Part of Grothendieck's program to define GT-like groups B_{ρ,σ} for arbitrary profinite quotients of SL2(Z)^ (including those where -1 is killed). This anticipates the genus-1 GT relations of the 1990s. The page itself, however, only performs routine bookkeeping with the det -1 involution.
missed.quote: on ne sait pas α̃ ∈ SL(2,Z)^, seulement α̃ ∈ GL(2,Z)^, de faire intervenir l'élément τ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Marginal: it documents that Grothendieck treated the orientation-reversing/complex-conjugation part of the genus-1 action, needed when μ ∈ Ẑ* is not 1. Later work by Nakamura and Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps addresses this independently.

deep.surprise_reason: Correct but routine group-theoretic setup: the det -1 involution of SL2 and the semidirect product. It interests mainly as context for the genus-1 'loop equation' program on the following pages.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: the struck-out 'en général' precedes 'on ne sait pas'; 'sait?' is a marginal insertion above 'pas'.
(24): ε0 = σ_𝔊 ρ_𝔊 = -σ_𝔊^{-1}ρ_𝔊 and ε1_𝔊 = ρ_𝔊σ_𝔊 = σ_𝔊(ε0_𝔊) = ρ_𝔊(ε0_𝔊) = -ρ_𝔊σ_𝔊^{-1}. Here x(y) means conjugation x y x^{-1}.
(27): the group symbol before '≝' is crossed out and rewritten. In view of the next page it denotes 𝔊' = {1,τ}.𝔊, not 𝔊 itself. The note '½ direct' means 'semi-direct'.
Left margin is roughly 'ce qui revient par la convention habituelle ... pour [?] passant...'. Its reading is uncertain.
Last sentence is probably 'Ceci dit, on va au mieux [?] paraphraser des constructions déjà faites par ailleurs.'
Page number on the sheet is 528.
